s0003.literal: Nine Princes of Emperor Wen; Twenty-nine Princes of Emperor Xuan; Eleven Sons of Houzhu
s0003.idiomatic: Nine Princes of Emperor Wen; Twenty-nine Princes of Emperor Xuan; Eleven Sons of Houzhu

s0004.literal: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons: the Deposed Emperor and the Prince of Shixing Bo Mao were born to Empress Shen; the Prince of Poyang Bo Shan and the Prince of Jin'an Bo Gong to Lady Yan the Honored Consort; the Prince of Xin'an Bo Gu to Lady Pan the Graceful Beauty; the Prince of Hengyang Bo Xin to Lady Liu the Bright Beauty; the Prince of Luling Bo Ren to Lady Wang the Filling Beauty; the Prince of Jiangxia Bo Yi to Lady Zhang the Cultivated Beauty; the Prince of Wuling Bo Li to Lady Han the Cultivated Beauty; the Prince of Yongyang Bo Zhi to Lady Jiang the Honored Consort; the Prince of Guiyang Bo Mou to Lady Kong the Honored Consort.
s0004.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had thirteen sons. Empress Shen bore the Deposed Emperor and Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing. Lady Yan the Honored Consort bore Bo Shan, Prince of Poyang, and Bo Gong, Prince of Jin'an. Lady Pan the Graceful Beauty bore Bo Gu, Prince of Xin'an. Lady Liu the Bright Beauty bore Bo Xin, Prince of Hengyang. Lady Wang the Filling Beauty bore Bo Ren, Prince of Luling. Lady Zhang the Cultivated Beauty bore Bo Yi, Prince of Jiangxia. Lady Han the Cultivated Beauty bore Bo Li, Prince of Wuling. Lady Jiang the Honored Consort bore Bo Zhi, Prince of Yongyang. Lady Kong the Honored Consort bore Bo Mou, Prince of Guiyang.

s0005.literal: Bo Gu's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.
s0005.idiomatic: Bo Gu's rebellion is treated in a separate biography.

s0006.literal: Two sons died young; this book gives no names.
s0006.idiomatic: Two sons died young; this book gives no names.

s0007.literal: The Prince of Shixing Bo Mao, styled Yuzhi, was Emperor Wen's second son.
s0007.idiomatic: Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing, styled Yuzhi, was Emperor Wen's second son.

s0008.literal: Earlier, the Founder's elder brother Prince Zhaolie of Shixing Dao Tan had served in Liang times as Direct Attendant of the Eastern Palace; in Hou Jing's rebellion he led two thousand crossbowmen to relieve the capital and died in the city from an arrow wound.
s0008.idiomatic: Earlier, the Founder's elder brother Dao Tan, Prince Zhaolie of Shixing, had served in Liang as direct attendant of the eastern palace. In Hou Jing's rebellion he led two thousand crossbowmen to relieve the capital and was killed in the city by an arrow.

s0010.literal: Collation variant: [Taiping]; second year, posthumously promoted to Palace Attendant, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the Three Dukes, commander of all military affairs in South Yanzhou and inspector of South Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as
s0010.idiomatic: Collation variant: [Taiping]; second year, posthumously made palace attendant, bearer of the staff with equal court ceremony to the three dukes, commander of all military affairs in South Yanzhou and inspector of South Yanzhou, and enfeoffed as

s0012.literal: [Changcheng County Duke], Editorial footnote marker 1. with posthumous title Zhaolie.
s0012.idiomatic: [Changcheng County Duke], [1] with posthumous title Zhaolie.

s0013.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, he again posthumously promoted him to Cavalry General-in-Chief, Grand Tutor, Editorial footnote marker 2. Governor of Yangzhou, changed the enfeoffment to Prince of Shixing Commandery, fief two thousand households.
s0013.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he again posthumously made him cavalry general-in-chief and grand tutor, [2] governor of Yangzhou, and changed the fief to Prince of Shixing, two thousand households.

s0014.literal: The prince was father to Emperor Wen and Emperor Xuan.
s0014.idiomatic: The prince was father to Emperor Wen and Emperor Xuan.

s0015.literal: Emperor Xuan had moved to the Guanzhong region at the end of Liang's Chengsheng era; by then the Founder remotely had Emperor Xuan inherit the fief as heir Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.
s0015.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had gone west to Guanzhong at the end of Liang's Chengsheng era. The Founder then had him inherit remotely as heir Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.

s0016.literal: In the sixth month of Yongding year 3 the Founder died; that month Emperor Wen entered to succeed the imperial line.
s0016.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yongding year 3 (559) the Founder died; that month Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne.

s0017.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan was still in Zhou and had not returned; Emperor Wen, because the main line lacked offerings, in the tenth month of that year issued an edict saying: "Of late the imperial foundation was first laid and fiefs and branches were planted; my own domain lies here, and a great state was opened especially for me.
s0017.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was still in Zhou and had not returned. Because the main line lacked offerings, in the tenth month of that year Emperor Wen issued an edict: "Of late the imperial foundation was laid and fiefs planted for kin; my own domain lies here, and a great state was opened especially for me.

s0018.literal: My younger brother Xu inherits and carries on the house sacrifices; though his territory was established, he has no means to offer them.
s0018.idiomatic: My younger brother Xu inherits the house sacrifices; though his territory was established, he has no means to offer them.

s0019.literal: Moreover our house met misfortune; mourning came early; the heir was far away and the returning carriage had not come back.
s0019.idiomatic: Moreover our house met misfortune and mourning came early; the heir was far away and the returning carriage had not come back.

s0020.literal: I unworthily with this slight person received this bright mandate, following the tortoise and tripod, my heart laden as on ice in a valley.
s0020.idiomatic: I unworthily with this slight person received this bright mandate, following the tortoise and tripod, my heart laden as on ice in a valley.

s0021.literal: Now that I have entered to serve the great lineage, the matter of princely libation is ended; the Shixing state temple has no one for its seasonal offerings—gazing on the frost and dew, I am moved to grief and anguish.
s0021.idiomatic: Now that I have entered to serve the great lineage, princely libation is ended; the Shixing state temple has no one for its seasonal offerings. Gazing on frost and dew, I am moved to grief and anguish.

s0022.literal: The heir Prince Xu is to be moved in fief to Prince of Ancheng; the second son Bo Mao is to be enfeoffed Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.
s0022.idiomatic: The heir Prince Xu is to be moved in fief to Prince of Ancheng; the second son Bo Mao is to be enfeoffed Prince of Shixing to maintain sacrifice to Prince Zhaolie.

s0023.literal: Grant throughout the realm one rank of nobility to those who are heirs to their fathers.
s0023.idiomatic: Grant throughout the realm one rank of nobility to those who are heirs to their fathers.

s0024.literal: Thus may boundless feeling be expressed and the mountains and rivers forever secured in blessing."
s0024.idiomatic: Thus may boundless feeling be expressed and the mountains and rivers forever secured in blessing."

s0025.literal: By old regulation when princes received enfeoffment, if they had not yet been given military titles they were not provided staff clerks; thereupon the eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "To increase and exalt emblematic titles and adorn carriage and dress is to make manifest their virtue and transform the people's expectations below.
s0025.idiomatic: By old regulation, when princes received enfeoffment without a military title they were not given staff clerks. The eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "To increase emblematic titles and adorn carriage and dress is to manifest virtue and transform the people's expectations below.

s0026.literal: The second prince, newly invested Prince of Shixing Bo Mao, in person honors the utmost pole, his spirit bright and keen; jade reflects at the killing hour, orchid fragrance at brocade years; pure splendor and fine reputation daily flourish and monthly rise; the Way is rich as Ping and He, his fame surpasses Gun and Zhi.
s0026.idiomatic: The second prince, newly invested Bo Mao, Prince of Shixing, in person honors the utmost pole; his spirit is bright and keen, jade reflects at the killing hour, orchid fragrance at brocade years; pure splendor and fine reputation daily flourish; the Way is rich as Ping and He, his fame surpasses Gun and Zhi.

s0027.literal: The imperial feeling pursues remembrance; sagely nature is heaven-deep; because the main line lacked succession he inherits and carries on the princely heir—though he received the jade and altars, his military patent was not conferred; how could this glorify sagely wisdom and favor the imperial branches?
s0027.idiomatic: The imperial feeling pursues remembrance; sagely nature is heaven-deep. Because the main line lacked succession he inherits the princely heir—though he received jade and altars, his military patent was not conferred. How could this glorify sagely wisdom and favor the imperial branches?

s0028.literal: We your subjects deliberated: he should be given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant and provided staff clerks.
s0028.idiomatic: We your subjects deliberated: he should be given the additional title general who pacifies the distant and provided staff clerks.

s0030.literal: Soon he was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in the two commanderies of South Langye and Pengcheng, and administrator of Pengcheng.
s0030.idiomatic: Soon he was made bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in South Langye and Pengcheng, and administrator of Pengcheng.

s0031.literal: In Tianjia year 2 his title was advanced to General Who Proclaims Favor and inspector of Yangzhou.
s0031.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 2 (561) his title was advanced to general who proclaims favor and inspector of Yangzhou.

s0032.literal: Bo Mao was clever and keen by nature, loved learning, was modest and respectful to men of worth, and because he was the crown prince's younger brother by the same mother Emperor Wen cherished him deeply.
s0032.idiomatic: Bo Mao was clever and keen by nature, loved learning, and was modest and respectful to men of worth. Because he was the crown prince's younger brother by the same mother, Emperor Wen cherished him deeply.

s0033.literal: At that time soldiers of the campaign-north army at Dantu illicitly opened the Jin tomb of Xi Tan and greatly obtained writings of Jin's Right General Wang Xizhi and traces of various famous worthies.
s0033.idiomatic: At that time soldiers of the campaign-north army at Dantu illicitly opened the Jin tomb of Xi Tan and greatly obtained writings of Jin's right general Wang Xizhi and traces of various famous worthies.

s0034.literal: When the matter came to light the writings were all confiscated to the county office and stored in the secret repository; Emperor Wen, because Bo Mao loved antiquity, gave many to him; thereby Bo Mao became highly skilled in cursive and clerical script and thoroughly obtained the Right General's method.
s0034.idiomatic: When the matter came to light the writings were confiscated to the county office and stored in the secret repository. Because Bo Mao loved antiquity, Emperor Wen gave many to him; thereby Bo Mao became highly skilled in cursive and clerical script and thoroughly obtained the Right General's method.

s0035.literal: In year 3 he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
s0035.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made general who pacifies the east, grand master with ceremonial parity to the three offices, and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

s0036.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Bo Mao was then in the capital; Liu Shizhi and others forged an edict to send out Emperor Xuan, and Bo Mao urged it to success.
s0036.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Bo Mao was in the capital. Liu Shizhi and others forged an edict to send out Emperor Xuan, and Bo Mao urged it to success.

s0037.literal: After Shizhi and the rest were executed, Emperor Xuan feared Bo Mao would stir the court; in Guangda year 1 he advanced his title to General of the Central Guard and ordered him to live within the forbidden quarters, exclusively associating with the Deposed Emperor.
s0037.idiomatic: After Shizhi and the rest were executed, Emperor Xuan feared Bo Mao would stir the court. In Guangda year 1 (567) he advanced his title to general of the central guard and ordered him to live within the forbidden quarters, exclusively associating with the Deposed Emperor.

s0038.literal: At that time the hopes of all within the seas turned to Emperor Xuan; Bo Mao was deeply discontent, day and night resentful, and repeatedly uttered vicious words; Emperor Xuan, because he was incapable, did not take it to heart.
s0038.idiomatic: At that time the hopes of all within the seas turned to Emperor Xuan. Bo Mao was deeply discontent, day and night resentful, and repeatedly uttered vicious words. Emperor Xuan, because he was incapable, did not take it to heart.

s0039.literal: When the man of Jian'an Jiang Yu plotted rebellion with Han Zigao and others, Bo Mao also secretly took part in the affair.
s0039.idiomatic: When Jiang Yu of Jian'an plotted rebellion with Han Zigao and others, Bo Mao also secretly took part.

s0040.literal: In the eleventh month of year 2 the Empress Dowager ordered the Deposed Emperor demoted to Prince of Linhai; that same day she also issued an order: "Bo Mao is frivolous; from his tender years he has failed stern instruction and ever more indulged fierce cunning.
s0040.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 2 the empress dowager ordered the Deposed Emperor demoted to Prince of Linhai. That same day she also issued an order: "Bo Mao is frivolous. From his tender years he has failed stern instruction and ever more indulged fierce cunning.

s0041.literal: Constantly by order of birth the younger brother next in line, he ought to hold state power; without limit to years and virtue he overstepped into wild arrogance, plotting disorder, stirring the palace apartments, summoning coarse danger, coveting the terrace offices; the heir lost the Way—hence this path of chaos; of all these vicious qualities he was chief plotter.
s0041.idiomatic: Constantly by order of birth the younger brother next in line, he ought to hold state power. Without limit to years and virtue he overstepped into wild arrogance, plotting disorder, stirring the palace apartments, summoning coarse danger, coveting the terrace offices. The heir lost the Way—hence this path of chaos. Of all these vicious qualities he was chief plotter.

s0042.literal: He should indeed be exhausted in that judicial district and this violent man punished by law.
s0042.idiomatic: He should indeed be exhausted in that judicial district and this violent man punished by law.

s0043.literal: Speaking of the imperial branches, I still harbor grief and anger; he is specially demoted to Marquis of Wenma; he should be placed under restraint and separately sent to his residence.
s0043.idiomatic: Speaking of the imperial branches, I still harbor grief and anger. He is specially demoted to Marquis of Wenma, placed under restraint, and separately sent to his residence.

s0044.literal: I did not expect this—my words increase in weeping and sighing.
s0044.idiomatic: I did not expect this—my words increase in weeping and sighing.

s0045.literal: Outside the Six Gates there was a separate lodge used as the place where princes received caps and married, called the Marriage Lodge; at this time Bo Mao was ordered to go out and dwell there.
s0045.idiomatic: Outside the Six Gates there was a separate lodge where princes received caps and married, called the Marriage Lodge. At this time Bo Mao was ordered to go out and dwell there.

s0046.literal: On the road he met bandits and perished in the carriage; he was eighteen.
s0046.idiomatic: On the road he met bandits and perished in the carriage. He was eighteen.

s0047.literal: The Prince of Poyang Bo Shan, styled Jingzhi, was Emperor Wen's third son.
s0047.idiomatic: Bo Shan, Prince of Poyang, styled Jingzhi, was Emperor Wen's third son.

s0048.literal: His appearance was imposing; his bearing leisurely and elegant; pleasure and anger did not show on his face; Emperor Wen deeply valued him.
s0048.idiomatic: His appearance was imposing; his bearing leisurely and elegant; pleasure and anger did not show on his face. Emperor Wen deeply valued him.

s0049.literal: In the Founder's time the realm was newly founded and the ritual and regulations for princes receiving enfeoffment were largely lacking; when Bo Shan received enfeoffment Emperor Wen wished to make the affair weighty; in the seventh month of Tianjia year 1, on bingchen, the eight seats of the Masters of Writing memorialized: "Your subject has heard that the root branch must be secure and the Zhou house's enterprise thereby enlarged; the bedrock boulder once set, the Han foundation thereby far-reaching—thus they could harmonize and proclaim the five cycles and regulate the hundred kings, firmly securing the numinous root and cloning fortune for generations.
s0049.idiomatic: In the Founder's time the realm was newly founded and ritual for princes receiving enfeoffment was largely lacking. When Bo Shan received enfeoffment Emperor Wen wished to make the affair weighty. In the seventh month of Tianjia year 1 (560), on bingchen, the eight seats memorialized: "We have heard that the root branch must be secure and the Zhou house's enterprise thereby enlarged; the bedrock boulder once set, the Han foundation thereby far-reaching—thus they could harmonize the five cycles and regulate the hundred kings, firmly securing the numinous root and cloning fortune for generations.

s0050.literal: The third prince Bo Shan displayed sagely virtue in his tender years and showed a singular bearing in his cap years; brilliance shone in the cinnabar side-chamber and radiance in the blue inner gate—yet the jade tablet was not held and gold and tin were not harnessed; how could this be ordering the great branches and establishing the princely kin?
s0050.idiomatic: The third prince Bo Shan displayed sagely virtue in his tender years and a singular bearing in his cap years; brilliance shone in the cinnabar side-chamber and radiance in the blue inner gate—yet the jade tablet was not held and gold and tin were not harnessed. How could this order the great branches and establish princely kin?

s0051.literal: We your subjects deliberated: he should be enfeoffed Prince of Poyang Commandery.
s0051.idiomatic: We your subjects deliberated: he should be enfeoffed Prince of Poyang.

s0053.literal: Thereupon he sent Attendant Cavalier at Large and Commissioner of Revenue Xiao Rui bearing the staff concurrently as Grand Mentor to announce at the Imperial Temple;
s0053.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent attendant cavalier at large and commissioner of revenue Xiao Rui bearing the staff concurrently as grand mentor to announce at the Imperial Temple;

s0054.literal: he also sent Master of the Five Armaments Wang Zhi bearing the staff concurrently as Grand Mentor to announce at the Altar of Soil and Grain.
s0054.idiomatic: he also sent master of the five armaments Wang Zhi bearing the staff concurrently as grand mentor to announce at the Altar of Soil and Grain.

s0055.literal: In the tenth month of that year the emperor came to the hall to bestow the investiture mandate, saying: "Alas!
s0055.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year the emperor came to the hall to bestow the investiture mandate, saying: "Alas!

s0056.literal: To establish the princely screen and assist and reward the royal house—reverently following the former canon, all must pass through this.
s0056.idiomatic: To establish the princely screen and assist and reward the royal house—reverently following the former canon, all must pass through this.

s0057.literal: You from youth have stood forth like jade and scepter, born knowing filial respect; Editorial footnote marker 3. your fine virtue enriches kinship, the unanimous praise of the gathered; to open a great state is truly the proper order of human relations—therefore I reverently follow the people's gaze and grant this jade and investiture.
s0057.idiomatic: You from youth have stood forth like jade and scepter, born knowing filial respect; [3] your fine virtue enriches kinship, unanimous praise of the gathered. To open a great state is truly the proper order of human relations—therefore I reverently follow the people's gaze and grant this jade and investiture.

s0059.literal: Strive to build your reputation and forever secure the ancestral altars—can you not be cautious?"
s0059.idiomatic: Strive to build your reputation and forever secure the ancestral altars—can you not be cautious?"

s0060.literal: When the mandate was finished he ordered princes and dukes and below all to feast at the prince's residence.
s0060.idiomatic: When the mandate was finished he ordered princes, dukes, and below all to feast at the prince's residence.

s0061.literal: He was then made General of the Eastern Center and administrator of Wu commandery.
s0061.idiomatic: He was then made general of the eastern center and administrator of Wu commandery.

s0062.literal: In year 6 he was made commander along the river, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of South Xuzhou.
s0062.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made commander along the river, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

s0063.literal: In Tiankang year 1 his title was advanced to General Who Guards the North.
s0063.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) his title was advanced to general who guards the north.

s0064.literal: His eldest son Junfan, in the Taijian era was invested heir of the Poyang state; soon he was made General of Manifest Prestige and administrator of Jinling; before he could inherit the title the Sui army arrived.
s0064.idiomatic: His eldest son Junfan, in the Taijian era was invested heir of the Poyang state; soon he was made general of manifest prestige and administrator of Jinling. Before he could inherit the title the Sui army arrived.

s0065.literal: At that time more than a hundred princes of the imperial house in the capital were there; Houzhu feared they would make trouble and summoned them all in, ordering them to encamp at the Court Hall and putting the Prince of Yuzhang Chen Shuying in overall command, while also secretly making preparations.
s0065.idiomatic: At that time more than a hundred princes of the imperial house were in the capital. Houzhu feared they would make trouble, summoned them all in, ordered them to encamp at the Court Hall, and put Chen Shuying, Prince of Yuzhang, in overall command, while also secretly making preparations.

s0066.literal: When the six armies were defeated they went out in succession to surrender and followed Houzhu into the passes.
s0066.idiomatic: When the six armies were defeated they went out in succession to surrender and followed Houzhu into the passes.

s0067.literal: Reaching Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui assigned them all to Longyou and the commanderies west of the river, each given fields and estates for settlement.
s0067.idiomatic: Reaching Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui assigned them all to Longyou and the commanderies west of the river, each given fields and estates for settlement.

s0068.literal: Earlier Junfan had been friendly with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zong; at this time Zong presented Junfan a pentasyllabic poem expressing the feeling of parting in another land—the words very bitter and keen; the literary men of the age all chanted and recited it.
s0068.idiomatic: Earlier Junfan had been friendly with vice director of the masters of writing Jiang Zong. At this time Zong presented Junfan a pentasyllabic poem expressing parting in another land—the words very bitter and keen; the literary men of the age all chanted and recited it.

s0069.literal: In Daye year 2 Emperor Yang of Sui took Houzhu's sixth daughter Nüyao as honored consort and loved her exceedingly; he therefore summoned the Chen clan's younger kinsmen all back to the capital and employed them according to talent—thereby they all became prefects and magistrates throughout the realm.
s0069.idiomatic: In Daye year 2 (606) Emperor Yang of Sui took Houzhu's sixth daughter Nüyao as honored consort and loved her exceedingly. He therefore summoned the Chen clan's younger kinsmen all back to the capital and employed them according to talent—thereby they all became prefects and magistrates throughout the realm.

s0070.literal: That year Junfan was made magistrate of Wen.
s0070.idiomatic: That year Junfan was made magistrate of Wen.

s0071.literal: The Prince of Hengyang Bo Xin, styled Fuzhi, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.
s0071.idiomatic: Bo Xin, Prince of Hengyang, styled Fuzhi, was Emperor Wen's seventh son.

s0072.literal: In Tianjia year 1 Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang returned from Zhou to court and died on the road; that year Emperor Wen installed Bo Xin as Prince of Hengyang to maintain sacrifice to the Xian prince.
s0072.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1 (560) Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang returned from Zhou to court and died on the road. That year Emperor Wen installed Bo Xin as Prince of Hengyang to maintain sacrifice to the Xian prince.

s0073.literal: Soon he was made General Who Proclaims Favor and governor of Danyang, with staff clerks provided.
s0073.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who proclaims favor and governor of Danyang, with staff clerks provided.

s0074.literal: In Taijian year 4 he was made General of the Central Guard.
s0074.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was made general of the central guard.

s0075.literal: In year 6 he was made General Who Proclaims Resolution and inspector of Yangzhou.
s0075.idiomatic: In year 6 (574) he was made general who proclaims resolution and inspector of Yangzhou.

s0076.literal: Soon he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant and Attendant Cavalier at Large.
s0076.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional posts of palace attendant and attendant cavalier at large.

s0077.literal: In year 11 his title was advanced to General Who Guards the Front, Editorial footnote marker 6. Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, the rest as before.
s0077.idiomatic: In year 11 (579) his title was advanced to general who guards the front, [6] grand mentor to the heir apparent, the rest as before.

s0078.literal: In Zhenming year 1 he went out as General Who Guards the South and inspector of Western Hengzhou.
s0078.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 (587) he went out as general who guards the south and inspector of Western Hengzhou.

s0079.literal: In year 3 when the Sui army crossed the river he and the Marquis of Linru Fang Qing were both killed by Eastern Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong, Editorial footnote marker 7. treated in Fang Qing's biography.
s0079.idiomatic: In year 3 (589), when the Sui army crossed the river, he and the Marquis of Linru Fang Qing were both killed by Eastern Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong, [7] treated in Fang Qing's biography.

s0080.literal: The Prince of Luling Bo Ren, styled Shouzhi, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.
s0080.idiomatic: Bo Ren, Prince of Luling, styled Shouzhi, was Emperor Wen's eighth son.

s0081.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Luling.
s0081.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 (565) he was installed as Prince of Luling.

s0082.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General of the Light Chariot, with staff clerks provided.
s0082.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general of the light chariot, with staff clerks provided.

s0083.literal: In year 7 he was transferred to General Who Exerts Might and General of the Central Army.
s0083.idiomatic: In year 7 (575) he was transferred to general who exerts might and general of the central army.

s0084.literal: Editorial footnote marker 8. Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of South Xuzhou.
s0084.idiomatic: [8] Soon he was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of South Xuzhou.

s0085.literal: In year 12 he was made General of the Left Wing and General of the Central Army.
s0085.idiomatic: In year 12 (580) he was made general of the left wing and general of the central army.

s0086.literal: In Zhenming year 1 he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant, Editorial footnote marker 9. Libationer of the National University, and concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
s0086.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 he was given the additional posts of palace attendant, [9] libationer of the National University, and concurrently supervisor of the heir apparent's household.

s0087.literal: In year 3 he entered the passes and died at Chang'an.
s0087.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the passes and died at Chang'an.

s0088.literal: His eldest son Fan had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangbin; in Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Ziyang.
s0088.idiomatic: His eldest son Fan had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangbin. In Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Ziyang.

s0089.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia Bo Yi, styled Jianzhi, was Emperor Wen's ninth son.
s0089.idiomatic: Bo Yi, Prince of Jiangxia, styled Jianzhi, was Emperor Wen's ninth son.

s0090.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Jiangxia.
s0090.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Jiangxia.

s0091.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General Who Proclaims Favor and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, with staff clerks provided.
s0091.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general who proclaims favor and inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, with staff clerks provided.

s0092.literal: Soon he was made General Who Proclaims Resolution, bearer of the staff, Attendant Cavalier at Large, commander of all military affairs in the two prefectures of He and Huo, and inspector of He.
s0092.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who proclaims resolution, bearer of the staff, attendant cavalier at large, commander of all military affairs in He and Huo, and inspector of He.

s0093.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10. In year 14 he was summoned as Palace Attendant, General of Loyal Martiality, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
s0093.idiomatic: [10] In year 14 (582) he was summoned as palace attendant, general of loyal martiality, and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

s0094.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the passes, was moved to Guazhou, and died on the road.
s0094.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered the passes, was moved to Guazhou, and died on the road.

s0095.literal: His eldest son Yuanji had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan; in Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Gushu.
s0095.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanji had earlier been enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan. In Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Gushu.

s0096.literal: The Prince of Wuling Bo Li, styled Yongzhi, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.
s0096.idiomatic: Bo Li, Prince of Wuling, styled Yongzhi, was Emperor Wen's tenth son.

s0097.literal: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Wuling.
s0097.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 6 he was installed as Prince of Wuling.

s0098.literal: At the opening of Taijian he was made General of the Cloud Banner, bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, and administrator of Wuxing.
s0098.idiomatic: At the opening of Taijian he was made general of the cloud banner, bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, and administrator of Wuxing.

s0099.literal: In the commandery he wantonly committed violence and plunder, driving and registering the people below, forcing seizure of goods—before and after they piled up; the common people suffered from it.
s0099.idiomatic: In the commandery he wantonly committed violence and plunder, driving and registering the people, forcing seizure of goods until they piled up; the common people suffered.

s0100.literal: In Taijian year 9 he was impeached by the relevant office; the emperor said the prince was young and had not yet attained the way of governance—it was all because the staff clerks could not correct and assist him; his military title was specially lowered; if hereafter he again offended, he would certainly be brought to law; if the relevant office did not speak up they would share the crime.
s0100.idiomatic: In Taijian year 9 (577) he was impeached by the relevant office. The emperor said the prince was young and had not yet attained the way of governance—it was all because the staff clerks could not correct and assist him. His military title was specially lowered; if hereafter he again offended, he would certainly be brought to law; if the relevant office did not speak up they would share the crime.
